Subject: Reserved capacity: topology & pricing questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the serving latencies looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a clear picture of how Redwood would structure reserved capacity for a customer like us. We're planning a 3-region deployment (us-west, us-east, eu-west) with the following rough profile:

- Steady baseline: ~160 concurrent inference streams (avg sequence length ~120 tokens)
- Expected sustained throughput: 45 qps overall, with 2x spikes during launches
- DR expectation: failover to a secondary region within 90s for critical routes

Questions we need answered before running an internal financing review:
1) Do you require separate reserved GPU pools per region or is a pooled/global commit available?
2) If separate pools are required, how do you price replication / warm standby capacity? Is there a fixed replication multiplier?
3) What explicit throughput guarantees (qps or tokens/sec) do you provide per reserved unit, and what are overage rates?
4) Are there cross-region routing costs or egress/replication fees we should budget for?

We'd like a ballpark commercial so I can feed to our procurement team and line up a term (12 vs 24 months). Can you send a short pricing framework and any assumptions?

Best,
Jane

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: topology & pricing questions

Jane — thanks, this is great context. High level answers up front, followed by a short pricing framework attached.

1) Topology: we offer two common patterns: separate regional reserved pools (recommended for residency/SLA isolation) or an active-passive cross-region routing model. Pooled/global commits across regions are supported only for hosted/Dedicated hybrid customers with specific network peering; for pure Dedicated with strict region isolation we do separate pools.

2) Replication / standby pricing: for separate pools we charge a replication standby fee expressed as a multiplier on the base reserved commitment. Typical multiplier is 0.25–0.5x depending on how much warm state you require (KV cache retention, pre-warmed instances). Active-active replication (both pools fully reserved) is priced at 1.0x per region.

3) Throughput guarantees: we guarantee per-pool throughput expressed as p50/p95 latency targets and a committed qps baseline per reserved GPU equivalent. Overage is charged at an incremental per-qps rate; for committed customers we offer a 10–20% buffer at no additional charge depending on term. Exact qps per GPU depends on model family/quantization; I attached a short sheet with example mappings and assumptions (seq length 120).

4) Cross-region routing & egress: routing itself has no separate per-request fee; replication/egress for warm standby storage is costed into the replication multiplier. Cross-region active traffic (serving from a region different from data residency) may incur standard cloud egress billed back to the customer — we can scope that if you share expected cross-region traffic volumes.

Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_3region_v1.pdf (pricing framework + example tables).

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement call this week so we can land on term and an initial commit level (we can model 12m vs 24m discounts). If you like, Ben can draft a simple SOW after we pick numbers.

—Tessa

Jane — thanks for the notes and for leaning toward 24 months. Final proposal below (summary) and I’ve attached the SOW + pricing PDF. We can push this into DocuSign once you confirm headcount/usage estimate.

Summary offer (24-month term):
- Topology: separate reserved pools per region (us-west, us-east, eu-west).
- Initial sizing: 8 GPU-eq per region (we'll run infra validation within 5 business days).
- Pricing: base reserved rate X per GPU-eq/month (detailed in attachment). Term discount = 18%.
- Replication multiplier: 0.25x for warm-standby (24m committed). This includes KV cache preservation and pre-warmed slots for faster failover.
- SLA & failover: p95 latency target = 180ms for the model family shown in the demo (seq len 120). Active-passive failover with automatic route flip within 90–120s; we provide a DR runbook and monthly failover test window.
- Overage: 1.5x on-demand pricing per qps beyond committed baseline; we include a 10% cross-region free buffer.
- Pooled commit path: eligible only after technical review; if eligible we can present a pooled pricing option that reduces total $ by ~6–8% vs separate-pool pricing, but it requires specific peering/networking and a signed Appendix.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the 24m term and the per-region headcount/usage estimate.

3) I'll upload the DocuSign bundle: https://www.docusign.com/ACME/Redwood-Dedicated-ACME-2026 and HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-DED-3REG
